extracted.intended_audience: philosophers of mathematics, mathematicians, and scholars interested in aesthetics and foundations of science
extracted.subtask_description: Articulating criteria for when a mathematical theorem or demonstration counts as 'beautiful' (e.g., enlightening vs. providing understanding) and explaining how such aesthetic judgments can play an epistemic role in mathematical discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rota's 'enlightening' criterion for mathematical beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: A piece of mathematics is beautiful when it is enlightening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rota stresses the relevance of mathematical beauty to research and claims beauty = enlightening, but (according to the article) stops short of explaining what he means by 'enlightening'. This functions as an evaluative standard but requires further explication to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beauty as providing understanding (Cellucci's alternative)
rubrics_metrics.description: A mathematical demonstration or theorem is beautiful when it provides understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper proposes this alternative approach to Rota: tie beauty explicitly to the capacity of a proof or theorem to yield understanding. This criterion applies to both demonstrations and theorems and suggests assessing whether the item increases the mathematician's grasp of why results hold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beauty as heuristic in discovery (guiding hypothesis selection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical beauty can guide the mathematician in selecting which hypotheses to consider and which to disregard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under this criterion, aesthetic judgments are treated as practical heuristics in the research process: beautiful structures or formulations direct attention toward promising lines of inquiry and away from less promising ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aesthetic factors have an epistemic role
rubrics_metrics.description: Aesthetic factors can have an epistemic role qua aesthetic factors in mathematical research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This asserts that aesthetic considerations are not merely psychological or rhetorical but can contribute to knowledge formation and justification in mathematics; evaluation should consider whether and how aesthetic features contribute epistemically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of beauty: demonstrations and theorems as loci
rubrics_metrics.description: Both mathematical demonstrations (proofs) and theorems are candidates for being judged beautiful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The criterion emphasizes that assessments of beauty apply at different levels (proofs vs. theorems), so evaluators should consider the kind of mathematical object (demonstration vs. theorem) when applying standards like 'enlightening' or 'provides understanding'.
